text.p: The Italian debt market ended mixed with cash bonds holding on to slim gains but Btp futures slipped into negative territory in the wake of other markets after U.S. treasuries fell on a strong June Chicago Purchasing Managers' index.
Btp futures had started off firmer, although taking in their stride Friday's Bank of Italy 50 basis point discount rate cut.

"The weak trend seen in the afternoon reflects above all a normal downturn in line with other weaker markets," one trader said. "But the underlying tone remains positive and the 10-year spread over Bunds is around 115 basis points," he noted.
"There hasn't been much action today ahead of the FOMC meeting Tuesday," another said, adding that attention is on U.S. jobs data out on Thursday ahead of the July 4 holiday on Friday.

"Volumes traded were only moderate today and this shows the downturn reflected a lightening of positions and not a real movement," one dealer said. "The further they fall, the more I believe the futures can rally again," he added.

"The September Btp contract should fall towards 133.50 to make a rise to 135.00 possible. If not, it will remain in the range between 133.90 and 134.40 until the FOMC outcome and U.S. non-farm payrolls Thursday," he said.
On the cash market, the February 2002 bond ended two basis points firmer at 99.96, yielding 6.86 percent. The spread was steady at 114 bps against 116 at midsession.
The lira was at day's highs against the mark as the German currency eased on jitters over the single European currency.

However, German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said after the market close that he was sure Germany would observe both the timetable and the entry criteria to join European economic and monetary union on time in 1999.
